Both molecules contain 6 carbons, 12 hydrogens and 2 oxygens, giving the same molecular formula of $\text{C}_6\text{H}_{12}\text{O}_2$.
Simplify $\text{C}_6\text{H}_{12}\text{O}_2$ to its simplest ratio and decide if an ester counts as a carboxylic acid to finish checking statements 2 and 3.
walkthrough:
**Find the molecular formula of each compound**

Both structures look long, so count carefully. You will find they both have the same atoms.

Left (hexanoic acid): $\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_2\text{COOH} = \text{C}_6\text{H}_{12}\text{O}_2$

Right (pentyl methanoate): $\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_2\text{OCHO} = \text{C}_6\text{H}_{12}\text{O}_2$

**Check statement 1 - structural isomers**

Structural isomers have the same molecular formula but different structural arrangements.

$$\text{same formula } \text{C}_6\text{H}_{12}\text{O}_2 \text{ + different connectivity = structural isomers}$$

**Check statement 2 - empirical formula**

Empirical formula is the simplest whole number ratio. Divide the molecular formula by 2.

$$\text{C}_6\text{H}_{12}\text{O}_2 \div 2 = \text{C}_3\text{H}_6\text{O}$$

**Check statement 3 - functional groups**

The left compound has $-\text{COOH}$, so it is a carboxylic acid. The right has $-\text{O-C(=O)-H}$, which is an ester group (a methanoate ester), not an acid.

So statements 1 and 2 are correct, but 3 is not.

options.A: This option claims 1, 2 and 3 are all correct. Statements 1 and 2 are true, but 3 is false because only the left molecule is a carboxylic acid, the right one is an ester.
options.B: This option states only 1 and 2 are correct. This is right because both share formula C6H12O2 with different structures, and both simplify to C3H6O, while statement 3 fails as the second compound is an ester.
options.C: This option claims 2 and 3 are correct. Statement 2 is true, but 3 is false. The H-C(=O)-O- group is the ester linkage of pentyl methanoate, not the -COOH of a carboxylic acid.
options.D: This option claims only 1 is correct. Statement 1 is true, but this misses that statement 2 is also true since C6H12O2 simplifies exactly to C3H6O for both compounds.
